sections.content: How many people stayed in Lytham St Anne's after gaining qualifications?

Lytham St Anne's is a medium-sized town in the North West. Lytham St Anne's does not have its own university.

Lytham St Anne's has medium levels of deprivation.

Overall, Lytham St Anne's ended up with:

  • fewer graduates than it produced
  • a similar number of non-graduates with advanced qualifications as it produced
Note: all towns and cities in this analysis are defined based on population size only. This means that some cities are classed as towns because of their population.

Let's explore this further

There were 1,410 state-school pupils from Lytham St Anne's who sat their GCSEs between the 2007 to 2008 and the 2010 to 2011 school years.

Of these, 640 (45%) went on to gain degree-level qualifications (level 6+ as defined by The Office of Qualifications and Examinations Regulation, or Ofqual ). We will call these people graduates.

Another 440 (31%) went on to gain other advanced post-16 qualifications, such as A-Levels, a foundation degree or higher apprenticeship (levels 3-5 as defined by Ofqual). In this tool, we will refer to these non-graduates with advanced qualifications as “qualified non-graduates", for brevity.

The charts below compare Lytham St Anne's to other English towns and cities using three measures:

  • what proportion of Lytham St Anne's' pupils became graduates or qualified non-graduates by the 2017 to 2018 academic year
  • of those graduates and qualified non-graduates, the percentages that lived in Lytham St Anne's in the 2018 to 2019 academic year
  • how many graduates and qualified non-graduates from elsewhere came to live there by 2018 to 2019, relative to the number who sat their GCSEs there

In some towns, some of this information may not be available because of small sample sizes.
The size and deprivation level of a town, as well as the qualification levels of older residents, were all related to students' educational attainment. Read our previous analysis.

Where did those who left Lytham St Anne's move to?

Of Lytham St Anne's's graduates, 255 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 35 of those graduates (14%) were living fairly locally, in the Blackpool travel to work area (TTWA).

Of Lytham St Anne's's qualified (level 3+) non-graduates, 135 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 50 of those qualified non-graduates (37%) were living fairly locally, in the Blackpool travel to work area (TTWA).

Of those in Lytham St Anne's' GCSE cohort:

  • 140 graduates left the North West
  • the most common region they moved to was London
  • 30 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates left the North West

In 2018 to 2019, 23% of graduates and 28% of qualified non-graduates living in Lytham St Anne's had moved there from elsewhere

In the 2018 to 2019 academic year, there were 470 graduates and 415 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates from our cohort living in Lytham St Anne's. This is compared with the 640 graduates and 440 qualified non-graduates who had lived there when they sat their GCSEs.

In 2018 to 2019, 77% of the graduates had also lived in Lytham St Anne's as GCSE pupils, while 23% had moved there from elsewhere.

Of the qualified non-graduates who lived in Lytham St Anne's in 2018 to 2019, 72% had lived there as GCSE pupils, while 28% had moved to the area from elsewhere.
